subject.title: [Feature Request]: Native Prompt Caching Support for Amazon Nova (Bedrock)

question: Should OpenClaw intentionally enable native prompt caching for direct Amazon Bedrock Nova models, including default short cache-point behavior, once live Nova proof is supplied?
rationale: Current source proves the requested behavior is missing, but enabling provider-side caching changes Bedrock Nova request shaping and default runtime behavior for existing users.

options.title: Land linked fix after live proof
options.body: Require redacted Nova Converse or ConverseStream proof, then accept the provider-owned policy change in the linked PR or a narrow replacement.

options.title: Require explicit opt-in
options.body: Preserve no-cache as the upgrade default and allow Nova cache points only through explicit user configuration or a narrower provider gate.

options.title: Defer Nova caching
options.body: Leave the current no-cache behavior in place until AWS proof, provider ownership, or user demand makes the default change less uncertain.

recommendation.title: Land linked fix after live proof
recommendation.body: Require redacted Nova Converse or ConverseStream proof, then accept the provider-owned policy change in the linked PR or a narrow replacement.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Amazon Bedrock provider cache-path work makes this the strongest available routing signal for the provider behavior choice.
